name: VOD Probe
description: Probes the real quality of each VOD relation (movies and every episode of every series version) with ffprobe in a background task and writes it into the relation's custom_properties, so every tool reading Dispatcharr's API can use it. Dry run by default.
author: oxios0x00

fields.label: Dry run (probe, but write nothing)
fields.help_text: ON (default): probes for real and reports what would be written. OFF: writes quality, resolution and probe into each probed relation's custom_properties.

fields.label: Movie/series relations per run (0 = all due)
fields.help_text: A run handles a random sample of this many due movie relations and series versions (a series version is one unit, all its seasons). 0 = everything due: use it for the big first pass, then let small daily runs pick up only what is new.

fields.label: Only these movie relation ids
fields.help_text: Comma-separated. When set, Probe Run probes exactly these relations, even if already probed. Leave empty for the normal selection.

fields.label: Only these series relation ids
fields.help_text: Comma-separated series relation ids (one per version of a series). When set, Probe Run handles exactly these, and no movies. Leave empty for the normal selection.

fields.label: Episodes: what to probe

options.label: One episode per series version, copied to all the others (recommended)

fields.help_text: Either way, every episode ends up with quality info. With one episode per series version, all the others get a copy of its result marked status 'inferred' (with inferred_from), assuming the files of a version are alike whatever the season; each version of a series (standard, 4K...) is sampled on its own. Cost, measured on a small sample: about 1.2 s per probe. One probe per version is about 900 probes for 900 versions (around 15 minutes) whatever the number of seasons, against one probe per episode (roughly 9 per version on the sample, several hours) for 'every episode'. Loading the episode list is needed in both cases: one provider request per series version, around 0.3 to 0.5 s each.

fields.label: Max concurrent probes
fields.help_text: Probing uses a real stream connection: stay below the provider's connection limit.

fields.label: Stop when the error ratio exceeds
fields.help_text: Checked after 5 probes. The run pauses itself instead of hammering a failing provider.

fields.label: Estimated seconds per probe
fields.help_text: Only used by Scan to estimate how long a full pass would take.

fields.label: Retry failed probes after (hours)
fields.help_text: A relation whose probe failed is offered again by Scan only after this delay.

fields.label: Max attempts per relation
fields.help_text: After this many failures a relation is left alone until Retry Errors is used.

fields.label: Probe timeout (seconds)
fields.help_text: ffprobe gives up after this delay.

fields.label: Estimated seconds per episode load
fields.help_text: Only used by Scan to estimate the duration.

fields.label: Schedule (5-field cron)
fields.help_text: 'minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week', for example '0 4 * * *' for every day at 04:00. Empty (the default) means no schedule: Apply then removes any existing one. A scheduled run handles everything due, whatever the per-run limit, so it is the small daily run once the big first pass is done. The settings are copied when Apply is clicked: click it again after changing any.

fields.label: Schedule timezone
fields.help_text: IANA timezone name. Empty means UTC.

actions.label: Probe Run
actions.description: Starts a background run that probes due movie relations and loads and probes series versions (see Episodes setting). With Dry run on it writes nothing and loads no episodes. The click returns at once; follow it with Run Status.

actions.label: Run Status
actions.description: Whether a run is going, its progress, or the result of the last one.

actions.label: Pause
actions.description: Stops the current run after the relation in progress and blocks new runs until Resume.

actions.label: Resume
actions.description: Lifts the pause (also set by the circuit breaker).

actions.label: Scan
actions.description: Counts the relations due for a probe and estimates the duration. Writes nothing.

actions.label: Coverage Stats
actions.description: Share of relations already probed, per type, with the quality tiers found.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Apply
actions.description: Registers or updates the periodic Probe Run from the schedule settings (and copies the current settings, Dry run included).

confirm.title: Remove the schedule?
confirm.message: Unregisters the periodic task. You can create it again with Apply.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Status
actions.description: Whether a schedule is registered and when it last ran.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Test Fire Now
actions.description: Runs the scheduled Probe Run now, as the timer would (everything due, no per-run limit).
